https://lean-lang.org/functional_programming_in_lean/Getting-to-Know-Lean/#getting-to-know
in this chapter, the book talks about an interactive mode, however it doesn't describe how to actually get there from anything? running lean just prints some help information, and I don't see a repl in there at all.
I saw this repository, however it's definitely not the thing described in the book; it uses some weird json syntax? https://github.com/leanprover-community/repl
how do I run lean in interactive mode?
https://lean-lang.org/install/ will help you setup a system using the Language Server Protocol, where you end up running Lean interactively from your code editor.
What would it look like? The "weird json" version is actually quite useful!
The amount of feedback that Lean gives when writing 1 line of Lean code is too much to usefully manipulate in the traditional repl-in-the-terminal sense.
I mean the book tells me to type #eval, #check etc, what I thought it was saying was to type those into some typical readline-like interface. similar to python's, node's, or haskell's.
But that only gives you < 3% of the interactivity that you would otherwise get.
The book does explicitly say to "write #eval before it in your editor", which looks something like this. But agree that it can be easy to miss!

zipsegv said:

is there no standalone repl?

There's https://github.com/leanprover-community/repl but it's intended to be used by other programs, not directly by humans.
